intro: Venice packs a beach town, one of LA's best restaurant streets and a handful of genuinely odd landmarks into a couple of square miles. Abbot Kinney and Rose Avenue carry most of the eating and drinking; the boardwalk, canals and skatepark carry the rest.

inf: The Infatuation: Best restaurants in Venice
infbars: The Infatuation: Best bars in Venice
tocoffee: Time Out: Best coffee shops in Venice
todo: Time Out: Things to do in Venice Beach
secret: Secret LA: Best breakfasts in LA

places.w: A tiny espresso bar a few steps off the boardwalk. People describe it as a friendly escape from the crowds, and the weekend line regularly spills onto the sidewalk.
places.o: Any espresso drink to go before a walk on the boardwalk.

places.w: Organic, house-roasted coffee from one of LA's best-known local roasters. Discover LA and longtime regulars point to the Rose Avenue shop as the Venice location worth the trip.
places.o: Drip coffee or a cortado.

places.w: An airy, lab-like coffee bar that holds one of the highest Foursquare scores in Venice. Regulars rate the coffee and warn that it's busy and very much a scene.
places.o: Pour-over, or an iced coffee for the walk down Abbot Kinney.

places.w: An espresso bar inside a custom motorcycle and surf shop. Visitors like browsing the bikes and boards while they wait.
places.o: Espresso, then a look around the shop.

places.w: A bright, plant-filled Australian-style cafe a block from the sand. It's known first for brunch, and coffee guides rank it with Venice's best.
places.o: Brunch with a flat white. Go early on weekends.

places.w: A bakery and deli with a big canopied courtyard that critics and locals both treat as a Venice essential. Expect a line and a hunt for a seat.
places.o: Tomato confit sandwich, tuna conserva, smoked fish and pastries.

places.w: A big, sunny all-day restaurant on Rose that locals use for long weekend brunches. It holds a strong Foursquare score across nearly 200 tips.
places.o: Weekend brunch on the patio.

places.w: The restaurant that put Abbot Kinney on the food map. Critics still rate its vegetable dishes and pizzas highly; expect it to be loud and packed.
places.o: A few vegetable plates and a pizza for the table.

places.w: A handmade-pasta house at the beach end of Abbot Kinney and one of the hardest reservations on the Westside. Reviewers single out the pastas and the focaccia.
places.o: Focaccia and two or three pastas to share.

places.w: An Abbot Kinney Italian classic that reopened after a long break and, by critics' accounts, kept its old energy.
places.o: Branzino with sweet peppers, gnocco fritto and spaghetti pomodoro.

places.w: An upscale Baja-style marisquería with bright, citrusy plates and tequila cocktails.
places.o: Rockfish ceviche with uni, shrimp aguachile and kanpachi al pastor.

places.w: A dim, lively izakaya that mixes traditional Japanese small plates with California produce.
places.o: Crispy pork belly gyoza, little gem salad with smoked shoyu and clam ramen.

places.w: Upscale Panamanian cooking that stands apart from the usual Venice menus, with a leafy patio and good cocktails.
places.o: Kanpachi steamed in banana leaf, shrimp dumplings in coconut bisque and twice-fried chicken.

places.w: A fun, casual seafood spot by the boardwalk, run by a team with its own fishing boat.
places.o: Bluefin tataki, clam and pork toast, whole fried fish, or the bacon-onion burger.

places.w: Loud, high-energy Thai with a sharp natural wine list.
places.o: Larb, fried chicken and a noodle dish.

places.w: A mariscos truck where lunch for one is cheap and the ceviche and cocteles are the reason people line up.
places.o: Ceviche tostada or a campechana.

places.a: Rose Ave, next to American Beauty
places.w: A roadside-style burger window that's quick, cheap and reliable.
places.o: The classic cheeseburger.

places.w: A candlelit bungalow on Main Street. Critics recommend it more for the romance and the wine list than for the pasta.
places.o: Squid ink linguine with lobster and a bottle of red.

places.w: Thin-crust pizza, rich pastas and a big patio a short walk from the sand. Book ahead on weekends.
places.o: Vodka sauce pasta, a thin-crust pizza and crispy branzino.

places.w: A classic steakhouse with a sunny front patio and strong cocktails.
places.o: Dry-aged porterhouse, potato pancake and a dirty martini.

places.w: A cozy, wood-paneled steakhouse that works for celebrations, though reviewers note service can run slow.
places.o: Dry-aged ribeye with truffle jus and wood-fired cabbage.

places.w: A long-running, dependable Mexican restaurant with a tableside tortilla station and a tequila cart.
places.o: Calamari steak, the birria burrito or build-your-own fish tacos.

places.w: An unpretentious beach dive open since the 1960s, with pool tables and a burger people swear by. Cash only.
places.o: A burger and a cold beer after the beach.

places.w: A nearly 70-year-old bar with a retro room, a patio and pool in back. Saturdays get busy.
places.o: A shot-and-beer combo.

places.w: A two-story bar steps from the sand with better bar food than it needs to have. Weekends are lively.
places.o: A pitcher upstairs at sunset.

places.w: A dim, bungalow-style cocktail bar with a patio that feels walled off from the traffic outside. Packed on weekends.
places.o: Fruit-infused cocktails.

places.w: A Tulum-style white room with a disco ball and genuinely good food at the bar. Walk-ins can usually grab a bar seat.
places.o: The Nomalizo (mezcal, watermelon, jalapeño) or a reposado espresso martini.

places.w: A bar that's more than 100 years old, with a Prohibition-era speakeasy downstairs that books live acts. It gets very loud.
places.o: A tequila cocktail upstairs, then the band downstairs.

places.w: A campy, fully committed tiki bar that feels like 1970s Waikiki. Reservations available.
places.o: Mai tais, a punch bowl for the group, or a tequila slushie in a coconut.

places.w: A small dance bar with 80s hits, a disco ball, inventive cocktails and natural wine.
places.o: The Passion (mezcal, hibiscus, passionfruit), then dance.

places.w: A sausage-and-beer hall with communal tables, imported beer and very good Belgian fries. Easy for big groups.
places.o: Order at the counter: two sausages and fries with dipping sauces.

places.w: The rooftop bar a block from the beach, one of the few on this stretch of coast. Reserve for sunset, even as a hotel guest.
places.o: Cocktails at golden hour.

places.w: Four blocks of canal houses and arched footbridges, and the calm counterpoint to the boardwalk.
places.o: Walk the loop. You can launch your own non-motorized boat from the Venice Blvd ramp.

places.w: The famous concrete bowls by the sand, often mid-video shoot. Watch from the fence.
places.o: Go near sunset for the best light.

places.w: The outdoor bodybuilding gym where Arnold trained. Fun to watch, and you can train there yourself.
places.o: Day passes run about $10.

places.n: Venice Beach Boardwalk and the Strand
places.w: LA's best people-watching, wide soft sand and the flat bike path that runs about 22 miles up and down the coast.
places.o: Rent a bike: Santa Monica is about 15 minutes north.

places.w: The legendary pickup courts by the boardwalk, where a lot of NBA careers got noticed.
places.o: Watch a run on a weekend afternoon.

places.w: Venice's most stylish street: boutiques, galleries, restaurants and bars along a walkable mile.
places.o: Artists & Fleas runs Saturdays 11am to 5pm at Abbot Kinney and Westminster.

places.w: A family-owned bookstore that's been on the boardwalk for more than 50 years, strong on local authors. There's a resident cat.
places.o: Buy a book and get a discount at the Sidewalk Cafe next door.

places.w: Two artists' home covered floor to roof in tile, paint and ceramics. Nothing else in LA looks like it.
places.o: Open Saturdays noon to 3pm by email reservation, about $20.

places.w: Street art everywhere, including the Touch of Venice mural on Windward that nods to Touch of Evil.
places.o: Start at Windward and Pacific and walk toward the beach.

places.w: A long, quiet pier at the south end of the boardwalk, good for a sunset walk away from the crowds.
places.o: Walk out at sunset, then a burger at Hinano across the street.
